Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the call this morning — a quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can close the technical qualification for our security team. High level: we need a Private/VPC-hosted deployment (no public inference endpoints) for production, with strict egress controls and auditability.

Key items:
- PII scope: account numbers (masked PAN), full names, email addresses, account metadata and transaction timestamps. No SSNs but there may be ancillary identifiers in free-text.
- Data residency: all production inference and logs must remain in EU (UK/EU acceptable) — no cross-border replication to US.
- Caching & persistence: we need confirmation that token/KV caches will not persist PII beyond the request lifecycle unless explicitly configured and that any persistent cache can be disabled.
- Logs & audit: immutable audit logs with at least 6 years retention for financial compliance; we also need streaming export to our SIEM (TLS syslog or S3) and field-level redaction options.
- Network/egress: outbound egress must be limited to allowlisted Redwood IPs/domains; no arbitrary outbound DNS resolution for customer data. For on-prem / air-gapped test beds, we may require the ability to install a connector inside our DMZ with no internet egress.

Can you confirm these are feasible / where you need more info? Also please attach any SOC2 / architecture diagrams and a short proposed mutual action plan for the security review.

Thanks — happy to schedule a 60-minute tech deep-dive next week if that helps.

Elena
Elena Park
Head of Cloud Security
ClearBank Solutions

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and for calling out the must-haves. Short answers below and next steps at the bottom.

Summary answers (short):
- Private deployment in a customer VPC (private endpoints + no public egress) — supported.
- EU-only residency: supported via region pinning and private control plane; we can restrict model artifacts, logs, and telemetry to EU regions.
- KV/token caches: default behavior is ephemeral per-request; persistent caches are opt-in and can be disabled for a tenant.
- Audit logs & retention: we support audit log export with configurable retention; 6+ years is available as an add-on (longer-term archival to customer S3 is supported).
- Egress: we support IP allowlisting and DNS restrictions; we can route through a customer-owned NAT or provide static egress IPs for allowlisting.

Next steps / action items (proposed):
1) I will share our SOC2 Type II and a high-level network diagram (attached).
2) Soojin (copied) will propose the specific network ports and egress IP ranges for your security ops.
3) Marissa will schedule a technical deep-dive (solutions + security) next week — proposed 60 minutes.
4) We'll prepare an initial mutual action plan (MAPP) with milestones for security review, deployment window, and compliance artifacts.

Would Tues 17th or Wed 18th (EU morning) work for the deep-dive?

Regards,
Aditya Rao

Elena / team — adding technical detail so your security ops can start a gap assessment. High-level confirmation first, then specifics we can use for your allowlist and SOC packet.

Technical confirmations:
- Private VPC model: Redwood Private supports a customer VPC connector (VPC peering or PrivateLink-style interface) so inference endpoints are reachable from your VPC only. No public ingress required.
- Egress patterns: outbound egress from the Redwoods' control plane to our telemetry endpoints can be disabled; inference traffic stays within the VPC unless you enable optional telemetry. For managed egress we provide a small set of static IPv4 ranges (we'll provide the list) and a DNS allowlist.
- On-prem / air-gap options: for fully air-gapped environments we support an on-prem package that runs the inference runtime locally. Where absolute no-internet is required, we offer a disconnected bundle and an S3-compatible import/export tool that your ops team can run over an internal network. This is typically delivered as a customer-managed VM/OCI image.
- Caching & persistence: KV/token caches are ephemeral by default; persistent caches are encrypted with customer KMS and require an explicit tenant opt-in. We can disable persistence entirely in your tenant config.
- Audit logs & retention: logs can stream to your TLS syslog endpoint, or be batched to your S3 bucket (server-side encrypted with your KMS). Immutable append-only logs are supported; retention policies are configurable (we can set 6 years). We also offer real-time forwarding to SIEMs (Splunk/Elastic) via secure channels.
- Field-level redaction: not automatic for LLM outputs, but we provide output post-processing hooks (webhook + redact service) that you can run in your VPC before persisting.
- Key management: we integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and external HSMs via KMIP for encryption at rest and envelope keys for model artifacts.

Network primer for allowlisting (example — subject to scheduling a diagram review):
- Protocols: HTTPS (443) for control/management plane; gRPC over TLS for streaming inference when using dedicated pools.
- Ports: 443 outbound for control plane; 123/UDP NTP optional for time sync if allowed; no inbound ports required to Redwood from your VPC.
- Egress IPs: Provide list during follow-up; we can also support NAT through your gateway so traffic appears from customer-owned IPs.

Attachments included here: sample ACL (clearbank-mapp-draft.xlsx) and our network diagram. I'll drop a hardened checklist and sample retention JSON for your compliance docs during the tech call.

If you want, Marissa can include a short runbook for the disconnected installer so your infra team can validate air-gap installation in a lab.

Soojin Lee
